qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Thierry Mariani (PfE) Subject:

On 16 January 2027, Nigeria is due to elect its President, according to the revised timetable published by its electoral commission (INEC). The EU is a major financial partner for that country: EUr 508 million has been allocated for the period 2021-2024 under the multiannual indicative programme, and EUR 39 million has been earmarked for supporting democratic governance during the 2022-2027 electoral cycle. However, the EU will be sending an election expert mission of only two to four people, having sent an observation mission comprising some 110 observers in 2023. At the same time, insecurity in a number of states and the discussions about the electronic transmission of results have fuelled doubts about the integrity of the election. In view of the above: 1.

Why is the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy forgoing a full observation mission and how can a team of no more than four experts provide credible monitoring in a country with more than 200 million inhabitants?
What measures is the Commission supporting to ensure election transparency and equal treatment of candidates (access to media, campaign funding and neutrality of the administration)?
What will it do to support voters’ access to the polls in areas affected by insecurity and will it review its funding in the event of serious shortcomings in the electoral process?
